Screened five bounded Texas candidates and added no route. Lake Nolte/Meadow Lake is officially closed; Palacios/Tres Palacios and Armand Bayou lack product-supported live-gauge numeric threshold packages; Lady Bird Lake and Lake Seguin are loop/lake route-shape blockers under the current point-to-point route policy.

screenedCandidates.blocker: TPWD currently says the Lake Nolte/Meadow Lake trail in Max Starcke Park East is closed to the public until further notice during GBRA spillgate/drawdown work, so access and safety gates fail before gauge or image review.

TPWD supports the new 10-mile one-way Tres Palacios River Trail and endpoint coordinates, but no product-supported live river/tide gauge with numeric route thresholds surfaced; wind, tide, bay exposure, and shipping/open-water safety are not scoreable under the current river-gauge policy.

TPWD documents an 11-mile reservoir trail with multiple loop options between Tom Miller Dam and Longhorn Dam, but the current route product requires a selected point-to-point river reach with numeric gauge thresholds; lake wind/water-level guidance and dam-bounded route shape are not enough to score safely.

TPWD documents Clear Lake Park and Bay Area Park accesses plus variable upstream/downstream route choices, but no product-supported live gauge or numeric tidal-bayou threshold package surfaced, and the route shape remains choose-your-own-distance rather than a bounded scored reach.

TPWD supports only a single-access no-shuttle loop/out-and-back on dammed Lake Seguin, with flow information referred broadly to GBRA; the current product lacks loop route-card support and no route-specific numeric threshold package was accepted.

Screened five distinct Texas candidates and added no route. All failed decisive publication gates before implementation: long-route/camping practicality, threshold support, endpoint coordinates/access, or loop route shape.

screenedCandidates.decisiveBlocker: Bounded screen found LCRA public access spacing and legacy La Grange-to-Columbus threshold support, but the practical route remains too long and thin for a new scored card: LCRA shows 34 miles from Buffalo Trail Park to Texas 71 Business Bridge Access, Houston Canoe Club reports the La Grange-to-Columbus run at 36 miles, and no manager source documents legal on-route camping or a normal overnight plan. Existing Plum-to-Buffalo and Columbus in-town cards already cover the strong same-day public-access portions without forcing a 34-plus-mile no-camping connector.

LCRA documents Beason's Park and Altair Boat Ramp Bridge as public lower-Colorado access points 20 river miles apart, and USGS 08161000 at Columbus is live, but no route-specific or clearly same-reach numeric paddling threshold surfaced for the downstream Columbus-to-Altair reach. The legacy table supports LaGrange-to-Columbus, not the next downstream segment, and community access notes did not supply a defensible gauge-calibrated floor/range.

TPWD Analysis of Texas Waterways and the legacy Texas River Flows table give unusually strong route and threshold support for the 25.5-mile Lavaca segment, and USGS 08164000 at Edna is product-live, but the endpoint coordinates/access anchors are not publication-ready. Navidad Community Crossing is described only as a county-road crossing off FM 822 nine miles northwest of Edna, and Old Vanderbilt Park is described textually near Lolita/Vanderbilt; no manager-grade endpoint coordinates surfaced, so adding the route would require manual coordinate inference.

The legacy Texas River Flows table lists San Bernard FM 422-to-Churchhill/Churchill with a 200 cfs minimum on the Boling gauge, and USGS 08117500 was product-live, but the route package lacks manager-grade point-to-point endpoint coordinates and access legality for the upstream FM 422 put-in. Churchill Boat Ramp has public ramp evidence, but the upstream access cannot be shipped from a road-crossing label alone.

TPWD documents Chandler Upper Neches as a no-shuttle loop/out-and-back style trail with up to eight miles possible from one access, not a selected point-to-point river reach. No route/gauge-specific numeric threshold tied to a product-supported live gauge surfaced, and recent public context still points to tree/downed-wood maintenance concerns. It does not fit the current scored point-to-point route gate.

blockers.blocker: TRPA documents a useful 4.8-mile Clear Fork run with numeric flow guidance, public launch names, and urban safety cautions, but USGS Water Services returned 503 for the candidate Clear Fork gauge checks during this run. The endpoint-coordinate package also remained incomplete for publication without manual access-anchor decisions, so the candidate failed the product-live gauge and coordinate gates before implementation.

TRPA describes this as an upstream/turnaround style White Rock Creek paddle rather than a normal scored downstream point-to-point card, with lack of proper put-ins/take-outs, common logjams or dragging, and E. coli / urban water-quality cautions. The minimum-flow guidance is non-numeric (almost always enough flow up to Skillman) even though an ideal band is given, so the candidate failed route-shape, public endpoint, and threshold gates.

TRPA gives promising East Fork Trinity threshold and gauge leads, including Forney, Crandall, and Rosser gauge context, but the bounded screen did not surface a selected manager-backed public endpoint pair with defensible coordinates, camping handling, and route-specific safety/access package. The candidate failed access, coordinate, and route-package gates before gauge validation was sufficient to implement.

This was a targeted recheck of the known retry condition. TPWD and TRPA route evidence and Sabine numeric threshold guidance remain promising, but USGS 08022120 still did not provide current product-live discharge during this run: stage values were current while discharge was stale to 2025-07-01. The route therefore still fails the product-supported live discharge / current-value gate.

TPWD provides strong endpoint coordinates, mileage, access, private-property, alligator, and flow-dependency caveats for Bevilport to Walnut Boat Ramp, but no route-specific numeric threshold tied to a product-supported live gauge surfaced. Because the route uses Angelina and Neches conditions in a reservoir-adjacent setting, assigning a gauge or threshold would require a policy/manual decision, so the candidate failed the threshold/gauge gate.

Screened five Texas coastal/new-trail candidates across the new Palacios TPWD trail family and Powderhorn Coloma Creek. No route was added because all candidates failed the current PaddleToday scored-river live-condition and numeric-threshold model, with additional route-shape, open-bay, wind/tide, shipping-channel, camping, and limited-shoreline-access blockers.

candidatesScreened.blocker: TPWD supports the new 10-mile one-way Tres Palacios River Trail from Carl Park Boat Ramp to East Bay Park with public access coordinates and notes limited camping at Carl Park and no camping at East Bay Park. USGS 08162600 was product-live at 38.1 cfs / 3.70 ft at 2026-08-12 07:30 CDT, but the selected route widens into Tres Palacios Bay and TPWD frames suitability around water level, tide, flow, and wind without publishing numeric cfs/stage thresholds. No accepted coastal/tidal route-scoring model exists for this river-to-bay transition, so the candidate fails threshold/live-condition policy before implementation.

TPWD supports the 1.5-mile one-way City by the Sea Trail between East Bay Park and South Bay Park with public access coordinates and no-camping statements at both parks. The trail follows the Palacios seawall through bay water and TPWD frames travel time around water levels, tide, flow rate, and wind. No product-supported live river gauge or accepted numeric coastal/tidal threshold model surfaced, so it cannot be scored as a PaddleToday river route.

TPWD supports the 2-mile roundtrip Palacios Wetlands Trail from East Bay Park into coastal salt marsh and wetland habitat, including a humpback bridge, a second lower bridge that may need portage in higher water, and a turn-around at the Highway 35 culvert. It is a same-access roundtrip marsh route, not a downstream point-to-point river reach, and no supported live condition adapter or numeric threshold model surfaced.

TPWD supports the 6-mile one-way Dolphin Run Trail from South Bay Park to Jensen Point with public access coordinates, but it crosses the Palacios shipping channel, rounds a private peninsula, and then crosses open Turtle Bay where TPWD warns strong winds and choppy water can occur. No product-supported live river gauge or accepted numeric wind/tide/bay threshold model surfaced, so the safety and condition gates fail before implementation.

TPWD supports Powderhorn as a four-trail shoreline/marsh system and lists the Coloma Creek Trail as an 8-mile roundtrip from the FM 1289 bridge, but says the creek behaves more like shallow bay water, includes mostly shallow mud flats, and is part of a coastal route-choice family with wind, tide, and access caveats. No product-supported live gauge or accepted numeric condition threshold model surfaced, so the route cannot be scored under the current river-route policy.

candidatesScreened.route: River Acres Park to Cypress Bend Park
candidatesScreened.blocker: The City of New Braunfels currently identifies River Acres Park and Cypress Bend Park as public Guadalupe River access parks, publishes recreation flow bands, says access parks are open 6am-midnight subject to high-water/public-safety closures, and says there are no lifeguards. USGS 08168500 returned live Guadalupe River data at New Braunfels (394 cfs / 2.46 ft at 2026-08-13 18:15 CDT), inside the city open-recreation band. The candidate still failed because the city page is an access/rules page, not a source-backed point-to-point paddling trail with route mileage, selected put-in/take-out sequence, route-specific thresholds, camping/no-camping terms for this exact reach, and safety package beyond general city rules.
candidatesScreened.retryCondition: Retry only if New Braunfels, TPWD, TRPA, or another manager-grade source publishes a specific River Acres-to-Cypress Bend point-to-point route package with mileage, endpoint handling, camping/no-camping terms, and threshold guidance tied to a product-supported gauge.

candidatesScreened.route: Canyon Dam to Cypress Bend / Gruene corridor
candidatesScreened.blocker: TRPA documents the below-Canyon Guadalupe corridor and current USGS Sattler/New Braunfels gauge context, and USGS 08167800 / 08168500 were product-live during this run. The candidate still failed because the manager evidence describes a long corridor (about 28 miles to Cypress Bend / 22 miles to Gruene) where lack of public launches and private-property access are the central issue; it does not provide a bounded day-route endpoint/camping/safety package that can be promoted without commercial/private access assumptions.
candidatesScreened.retryCondition: Retry only if a manager-grade source publishes a bounded public-access split in this corridor with exact public endpoints, camping/no-camping terms, safety hazards, and supported thresholds; do not infer access through outfitters or private resort property.

candidatesScreened.route: Trophy Trout Waters: Fourth Crossing to Second Crossing
candidatesScreened.blocker: Fresh TPWD and GRTU checks did not clear the known Trophy Trout blocker. TRPA supports the 7-mile reach, but access evidence remains fishing/lease/outfitter oriented: TPWD leased fishing access is for bank fishing and non-motorized watercraft for fishing during lease hours, while GRTU LAP access requires membership and uses private locations. That fails the general public paddling endpoint, camping/no-camping, and route-safety package gates despite product-live Guadalupe gauges.
candidatesScreened.retryCondition: Do not retry unless a public manager publishes a non-lease public paddling endpoint pair and exact route package for the Trophy Trout reach, including camping/no-camping and safety terms.

candidatesScreened.route: Bob Bryant Park to Bastrop Fisherman's Park
candidatesScreened.blocker: LCRA identifies Bob Bryant Park and Bastrop Fisherman's Park as consecutive public lower-Colorado access points with coordinates and about one mile of separation. The candidate failed because it is a very short connector contained within existing Bastrop Colorado River coverage; the current inventory already ships Utley-to-Fisherman's Park and Fisherman's-to-Lost Pines cards with the practical Bastrop trail story, gauge, threshold, no-image, camping, safety, coordinate, and geometry packages. A one-mile Bob Bryant connector would not add a materially distinct Google-searchable route.
candidatesScreened.retryCondition: Do not retry unless a manager publishes a distinct official Bob-Bryant-specific route with separate thresholds, safety/camping terms, and user value outside the shipped Bastrop chain.

candidatesScreened.route: River Bend Boat Ramp to Matagorda Bay Nature Park
candidatesScreened.blocker: LCRA identifies River Bend Boat Ramp and Matagorda Bay Nature Park as consecutive lower-Colorado access points five miles apart, with River Bend one mile downstream of the Intracoastal Waterway and providing access to the last six miles of the Colorado River, the ICW, and portions of Matagorda Bay. The candidate failed because it is a coastal/ICW mouth segment without a defensible route-specific live river threshold model: USGS 08162500 near Bay City had current stage but discharge remained stale from 2026-08-01 during this run, and the source package does not separate river-current decisions from ICW/bay/wind/tide hazards or publish legal route camping terms.
candidatesScreened.retryCondition: Retry only if a manager-grade source publishes a river-only lower-Colorado mouth route with supported current gauge/threshold guidance, explicit wind/tide/ICW safety handling, endpoint coordinates, and camping/no-camping terms.
